summary.text: A Caucasian man from Wisconsin was referred to the hospital for evaluation of iron deficiency anemia, palpitations, dizziness and right calf discomfort that developed progressively over two weeks, with mild dizziness and intermittent mild shortness of breath. He had a history of intermittent heartburn relieved by calcium carbonate, took no prescription medications, did not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs, and denied prior malignancy or venous thromboembolism. His parents and siblings were healthy.

He was afebrile and tachycardic at 103 beats per minute, with severe iron deficiency anemia, negative fecal occult blood, normal liver function tests and undetectable troponin I. Doppler showed extensive right leg deep vein thrombosis and CT showed bilateral pulmonary emboli, greater on the right, with septal flattening suggesting right heart strain. Echocardiography showed a mild decrease in right ventricular ejection function. Hypercoagulability work-up and abdominal CT were unrevealing; IV heparin was followed by apixaban.

Celiac serology was positive and markedly elevated, HLA-DQ2 and DQ8 were positive, and EGD showed absent duodenal folds with flattened mucosa. Duodenal biopsy showed partial villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes consistent with celiac sprue, Marsh 3B, and colonoscopy was normal. He was started on a gluten-free diet and prescribed iron supplements for 3 months.

Three months after the diagnosis his hemoglobin, iron and ferritin had normalized; he continued the gluten-free diet and had no adverse effects from anticoagulation. The authors planned long term aspirin 81 mg daily after completing anticoagulation and would use lifelong anticoagulation if DVT recurred.

evidence.quote: Laboratory studies showed severe iron deficiency anemia (Hgb: 91 g/dL, MCV: 60 fL, iron: 14 mcg/dL, iron saturation: 4%, TIBC: 369 mcg/dL, and ferritin: 7 mcg/dL).

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not correct the value or unit; do not infer 9.1 or g/L.

ambiguities.issue: The case text says apixaban was given for long term anticoagulation, while the discussion says the authors decided to anticoagulate for 6 months; "long term" is qualitative, so this is an ambiguity rather than two conflicting numbers, and the source does not relate the two statements.

evidence.quote: For his pulmonary embolism, he has been placed on long term anticoagulation using apixaban.
We decided to anticoagulate our patient for 6 months using the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile or choose a duration.

ambiguities.issue: The clause "that started on the day of presentation" certainly covers the shortness of breath (its nearest noun) but may or may not also cover the dizziness, while the preceding sentence says the listed symptoms developed over two weeks.

evidence.quote: He was complaining of mild dizziness and intermittent mild shortness of breath that started on the day of presentation.
His symptoms progressively developed over a period of two weeks before presentation.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign an onset on the day of presentation to dizziness.

ambiguities.issue: The three-month follow-up is anchored to "the diagnosis", which the sentence does not name; the only diagnosis described in that paragraph is the biopsy diagnosis consistent with celiac sprue, and the order of the biopsy diagnosis before the follow-up relies on that reading.

evidence.quote: Three months following the diagnosis, his hemoglobin, iron, and ferritin levels have normalized.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a calendar date to the diagnosis or to the follow-up.

ambiguities.issue: The unit is not printed after the anti-tissue transglutaminase IgG value of 60.1 or after the white cell count and platelet count; only the reference range of the antibody carries a unit.

evidence.quote: Serologic studies for celiac disease revealed positive and significantly elevated antibodies: anti-gliadin IgA (>150 units, normal range < 20 units), anti-gliadin IgG (81.5 units, normal range < 20 units), anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (127.3 units, normal range < 15 units), anti-tissue transglutaminase IgG (60.1, normal range < 15 units), and positive IgA endomysial antibodies (1 : 80 titer).
Other laboratory studies included WBC: 5.8, Plt: 269, and INR: 1.1.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not add units to these values.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the patient was admitted and the case text says he was referred to the hospital; no admission date, length of stay or discharge is stated.

evidence.quote: was admitted for shortness of breath
was referred to our hospital for further evaluation of iron deficiency anemia, palpitations, dizziness, and right calf discomfort

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a length of stay, ward course or discharge.

ambiguities.issue: The hypercoagulability work-up including homocysteine levels revealed no abnormalities, and the discussion says the patient had normal folic acid and homocysteine levels; the source does not say whether the discussion refers to the same homocysteine measurement.

evidence.quote: Extensive work-up for hypercoagulability revealed no abnormalities.
this does not apply to our patient who had normal folic acid and homocysteine levels

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two statements into one measurement or count them as two measurements.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the three JPEGs were inspected separately in visual.json.
The abstract and the case presentation print different ages (46 versus 48 years) and differ on chest pain; both sides are kept review_only.
Hemoglobin is printed as 91 g/dL; kept as printed, probably a print artefact.
Table 1 and most of the discussion concern 19 published literature cases and are not index patient facts; no table of the index patient is printed, so no measurement series applies.
Authors hypotheses about mechanism (severe inflammation as procoagulant state) and statements that the patient lacked traditional risk factors are interpretation and are not recorded as facts.
No dates, admission or discharge details, doses of heparin or apixaban, or follow-up beyond three months are stated.
